label: text
text: TROOPS RUSHED UP.

label: text
text: Peking, Nov. 2.

label: text
text: Lungchow is in Kwangsi province, near the boundary separating China and India-China. It should not be confused with a minor town or the same name in Kwangtuhr province.

label: text
text: Bandits killed the French Consul M. Robert, of Bungchew, on October 31, while he was motoring from there to Bangson, in Indo-China. — Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text:
Body Found in Grove.
Lutei

label: text
text: M. Robert was accompanied by Monsieur Cadet, an administrator in the French Colonial service. The gang of bandits or pirates attacked them 25 kilometres from Lungchow in Kwangsi province whence they had started early in the morning.

label: text
text:
The Chinese authorities, on hearing the news, sent a battalion of troops who arrived on the spot at two of the afternoon and found Mr. Roberts's corpse in a grove, pierced by two bullets in the head and stomach.
M. Cadet and the Annamite ahuffear were dragged away by the bandits but managed to escape and after 24 hours' exhausting walking arrived safely at the French Consulate at Lungchow on the night of Nov. 1.

The Levy Proposal.
To-morrow representatives of all the Trades Unions will meet to consider the miners' proposal for a levy. It is considered that negative decisions both in regard to an embargo and in regard to a levy are foregone conclusions, and it is expected that when the miners' delegates assemble in London later in the week these negative decisions will have an important effect.
